  • ThinkingSummaryMistral released Mistral Large 4 (Le Chonk), a 1-trillion-parameter multimodal model, now available with improved coding, cybersecurity, and reasoning efficiency. It leads open-weight benchmarks in coding and defensive security while offering three reasoning modes for cost-performance balance. Fully open-weight and European-trained, it empowers sovereign AI with customizable, self-hosted deployment options.We release the weights of Le Chonk, advancing the frontier of open models in agentic coding and cybersecurity.Earlier this month, we released Mistral Large 4 (Le Chonk), our flagship 1-trillion-parameter, natively multimodal model, in public preview. Gains continue to accelerate, with no signs of saturation.Today, we're releasing the weights of this improved Mistral Large 4. The new model also features substantial gains in reasoning efficiency that give developers greater performance while lowering inference costs.Mistral Large 4 ranks as the best open-weight model for coding and among the world's most capable open models overall. By partnering with Mistral AI, our ambition is to combine the best of human expertise and digital technology to deliver an enhanced experience of both customers and employees over the long term.Zakaria Moursli, Executive Vice President, Operational Performance, Payments and Digital Services, La Banque PostaleSee it in ActionCyber Vulnerability Triage: an agent reads incoming vulnerability reports, investigates the source code and product context, reproduces the flaws in an isolated sandbox, then writes and iterates on a patch until a canary exploit no longer works.Agentic webdev: with no human help, Mistral Large 4 builds Orbital Trace, a live 3D map of roughly 19,000 satellites and debris pieces orbiting Earth. It pulls real tracking data, writes the app, uses it in a browser to catch its own bugs and slowdowns, then fixes what an independent reviewer flags until all requirements pass.Quantum chemistry solver: Mistral Large 4 writes, from scratch, software that calculates where electrons sit in a molecule, and checks its answers against a standard chemistry tool. It then builds a 3D page around it: pick a molecule such as benzene or water, drag a slider to pull it apart, and watch the electrons regroup as the bond breaks.Built for Sovereignty.As organizations build AI around their knowledge and workflows, sovereignty means that they retain control of the models they depend on and the intelligence they create. With Mistral Large 4, that control begins with the model itself. Organizations have the ability to inspect, customize, and deploy the model on their own infrastructure. They can use and improve Mistral Large 4 without depending on Mistral to serve it through an API. Mistral Large 4 was developed and trained from scratch in Europe, giving organizations clarity about the origins of the technology they’re building on. Control also extends to how AI operates inside an organization. Organizations can customize Mistral Large 4 around their proprietary data with Mistral Forge, and they can build, govern, and improve the resulting agents and applications using Mistral Studio. Mistral’s Applied AI experts can work alongside customer teams to build and deploy these tailored systems. Through that work, teams understand the architecture and decisions behind what they’ve built, along with the methods used to train and operate it, so they can run and improve their AI independently. Sovereignty does not always require self-hosting; sometimes it just requires deployments that meet your control requirements. For organizations that prefer a managed service, Mistral Large 4 is available through Microsoft Foundry, with private deployment options for Azure developers.Microsoft and Mistral AI share a commitment to expanding customer choice in next-generation AI. As the first cloud provider to bring Mistral Large 4 to customers, Microsoft is making Mistral’s latest open-weight model available through Microsoft Foundry, an enterprise AI platform built for evaluating, deploying, and operating models at scale. For organizations advancing sovereign AI strategies, this combination offers greater flexibility and control across their data, infrastructure, and AI operations.Tina Schuchman, Corporate Vice President, Foundry, Microsoft Start building with Le ChonkMistral Large 4 is available to try, deploy, and customize today.Get started in Mistral Studio, through the Mistral API, or on OpenRouter. For full control, download the open weights from Hugging Face and deploy on your own infrastructure with vLLM or SGLang. The model card and license have everything you need to get started — and for those who want to go deeper, a full technical report is coming soon.You can also try the new model in Vibe Code; give it a feature to build or a bug to fix in your own repository.Mistral Large 4, is also available through NVIDIA-hosted endpoints, as an optimized NVIDIA NIM container for serving with vLLM. Developers can use the open source NeMo AutoModel library for customization or the open source TensorRT LLM library for high-throughput serving.Enterprises can also tailor Mistral Large 4 to their proprietary data, use cases, and guardrails with Mistral Forge. Talk to our team to learn more.The model is available to use under the Mistral Ecosystem Open-Weight license, a modified MIT license. The model is free to use, modify, fine-tune, and commercialize, with a single condition: businesses that operate a Model-as-a-Service offering must obtain a separate commercial license from Mistral before using the model commercially.Starting today, Mistral Large 4 is priced at $0.70 input / M, $0.07 cached input / M, and $2.10 output / M tokens.We encourage the community to put Mistral Large 4 to the test. Run your own evaluations, push its limits, and share your findings with us on X, Discord, or GitHub.What's NextMistral Large 4 will serve as the foundation for a new generation of specialized and optimized Mistral models. Building on recent releases such as Voxtral and Timestral, we'll continue expanding the frontier of open-weight AI, continuing to give developers and enterprises greater freedom to build, customize, and own their intelligence.

jacquesm 2026/10/30 07:49
不，如果一个模型在基准测试中得分良好，那么可能是它们进行了benchmaxxed，如果现代模型在基准测试中得分较差，那么它可能是一个非常糟糕的模型，但几乎可以肯定它没有进行benchmaxxed。让模型在特定基准上表现良好相对容易，不关心这一点的公司更有机会制作出总体上表现良好的模型，因为调整基准模型通常会以牺牲其他东西为代价。

我在没有外人见过的数据上运行自己的基准（不幸的是，这个模型太大了，所以不会在这里发生），这有时会给出与您在考虑各个基准站点时所期望的顺序不一致的结果。当然，我们的基准完全有可能不具有代表性，但它似乎可以很好地预测哪些模型对我们有价值，哪些模型对我们没有价值。最近，我们研究了一个被大量炒作的模型，在我的一生中，我们无法让它的性能接近已发布的基准，而我们用于控制的模型绝对在误差范围内。它并不总是同样一成不变。

No, if a model scores good on benchmarks it could be that they have benchmaxxed, if a modern model scores bad on benchmarks it could be a really bad model but it almost certainly isn't benchmaxxed. It's relatively easy to make a model do well on particular benchmarks, companies that don't care about that stand a better chance at making a model that does well in general because tweaking a model for benchmarks usually is at the expense of something else.

I run my own benchmarks (this model is - unfortunately too large so that won't be happening here) on data that no outsider has ever seen and this gives sometimes results that are not in line with the order that you would expect if you took the various benchmark sites into account. It is of course entirely possible that our benchmark is not representative but it seems to work quite well as a predictor for which models have value for us and which do not. Recently we looked a model that has been pushed with a significant amount of hype and for the life of me we could not get it to perform even close to the published benchmarks, whereas the models we used for controls were definitely within the margin of error. It's not always equally cut-and-dry.
